subject: Request for subprocessor inventory + KMS ownership details
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@baxterhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: security@baxterhealth.com
Date: 2026-04-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vendor questionnaire - subprocessor inventory and crypto ownership

Hi Aditya,

Baxter is running a security intake for an upcoming engagement; our procurement and infosec teams need a current subprocessor inventory and supporting evidence so we can complete the SIG/CAIQ and SOC 2 mapping. Specifically we need the following by EOD next Thursday (5 business days):

- A CSV of current subprocessors with role/function, country of operations, and retention/residency notes (we need to know if any subprocessors persist PII outside the US).
- SOC 2 Type II report (or AICPA bridge letter) covering production services.
- Architecture or dataflow diagram showing where customer data traverses (include any 3rd-party caches or analytics endpoints).
- KMS/cryptography ownership model: are keys customer-managed (BYOK) or Redwood-managed? If both options exist, please list which deployment types they apply to (hosted/dedicated/private).
- High-level summary of subprocessor onboarding controls (background checks, contractual security requirements, right-to-audit).

Where possible, bundle attachments as single PDFs/CSVs and flag anything that is export-controlled or has restricted distribution. If any of the items above will take longer, let me know what you can provide within five days and a realistic ETA for the remainder.

We may redact limited commercial terms, but we need the security-relevant assertions to be complete for our legal/compliance review.

Thanks,

Samira Khan
Sr. Information Security Manager
Baxter Health

+1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Vendor questionnaire - subprocessor inventory and crypto ownership

Samira — thanks for the clear list. We can get most of this over within the timeline; attaching the initial exports for your review. Quick notes up-front:

- Attached: redwood_subprocessor_inventory_20260419.csv (includes name, role, country, and whether the subprocessors handle tokens/PII).
- Attached: SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2023.pdf (redacted report: control descriptions and test results; we can provide an auditor contact under NDA if you need the unredacted binder).
- Attached: dataflow_diagram_redwood.drawio.png (annotated for customer-data paths; highlights caching and 3rd-party telemetry endpoints).

Open questions from our side to make sure we map correctly:
1) When you say "PII" — can you confirm the classification threshold Baxter uses (e.g., names/email only vs. health identifiers)? We want to mark subprocessors appropriately.
2) Do you require evidence of background checks for all subprocessors (contractors included) or only for those with privileged access?

Short answer on KMS: Redwood operates a mixed model — details depend on deployment. I'll outline the high-level options in a follow-up message once you confirm how deep you want the implementation details (e.g., HSM vendor + key rotation windows). If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute sync with myself and Jonas (security) to walk through the inventory.

Attaching: redwood_subprocessor_inventory_20260419.csv, SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2023.pdf, dataflow_diagram_redwood.drawio.png

Best,

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@baxterhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: security@baxterhealth.com
Date: 2026-04-20T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor questionnaire - subprocessor inventory and crypto ownership

Thanks Aditya — received the CSV and SOC2. A couple follow-ups after a quick pass:

- PII classification: Baxter treats name/email as low-sensitivity, PHI/health identifiers as high-sensitivity. Please flag subprocessors that process or persist PHI explicitly.
- Background checks: we require vendor attestations for background checks on anyone with privileged access (ops, SRE, support that can access production). For contractor-level non-privileged roles, a statement of policy is usually sufficient.
- KMS: we need to know two things in writing: (1) whether Redwood stores customer keys in a Redwood-managed HSM for Hosted customers, and (2) is there a BYOK or customer-managed key option for Dedicated/Private? If BYOK exists, we need details on supported KMS vendors and an outline of key import/export restrictions.

Also: please provide your subprocessor onboarding summary (controls and contractual clauses) and a brief note on whether Redwood uses subprocessors for telemetry/analytics where sample-level metadata might be retained.

If you can provide the KMS ownership matrix and a short onboarding summary today, that would be ideal. Otherwise, propose a time for the 30-minute call and we'll make sure our security SME is available.

Regards,
Samira

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@baxterhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-21T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor questionnaire - subprocessor inventory and crypto ownership

Samira — quick follow-up with the details you requested. Answers below and attached files for your records. Forwarding Jonas for any deeper crypto questions.

1) PHI flagging: the attached CSV includes a "PHI_handling" column; rows flagged "yes" indicate subprocessors that may process or persist PHI for certain customers. We noted the relevant services in the notes column.

2) Background checks and onboarding: see subproc_onboarding_summary.pdf (attached). In short: privileged-access subprocessors undergo identity verification, enhanced background screening (employment + criminal checks where local law permits), SCIM-based least-privilege provisioning, and contractual SLAs that include SOC 2/ISO obligations, breach notification timelines, and right-to-audit clauses. Contractor non-privileged roles are covered by our vendor policy and documented in the summary.

3) KMS/cryptography ownership (see kms_ownership_matrix.xlsx):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Default is Redwood-managed keys protected in an HSM service (FIPS 140-2 level where applicable). We also offer BYOK for enterprise customers via an approved KMS import path; supported vendors: AWS KMS (customer master keys), Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault. BYOK requires a short onboarding checklist and an HSM import artifact; we cannot export keys once imported into a Redwood-managed KMS unless the customer exports prior to import.
- Dedicated: Typically customer-managed option available (customer provides keys via KMS integration or brings own HSM into the VPC). If the customer opts for Redwood-managed keys, similar terms as Hosted apply.
- Private / On-prem: Customer fully controls keys (customer-managed). Redwood installs connectors for local KMS/HSM; key material never leaves customer-controlled infrastructure.

4) Telemetry/analytics subprocessors: We use a small set of telemetry processors for usage metrics and crash reporting; none store full request payloads. The inventory marks these services and the retention windows. If Baxter needs telemetry excluded entirely, we can add a contractual clause and technical controls for suppression at the route level.

5) Next steps: attaching kms_ownership_matrix.xlsx and subproc_onboarding_summary.pdf. Also linking our CAIQ mapping and the Mutual Action Plan template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cREDWOOD-CAIQ-MAPPING (view-only unless shared).

Would you like to schedule the 30-minute sync tomorrow morning PST? Jonas and I can join and run through any technical questions.

Thanks,
Aditya
